notes: PLACEHOLDER TUNING (mw-e09.4), to tune in play. Offsets are dB relative to stone (0), kept in the order the audio bible §7.3 requires: carpet < grass < dirt < stone < wood-hollow < gravel / water / metal-grate / bone < glass-shards. Carpet is −10 dB (the bead). Quiet and soft surfaces (carpet −10, grass −5, mud −4, straw −4, dirt −3, snow −2) muffle a step; wood is +2 and hollow wood (bridges, upper floors) +5; loose or ringing surfaces are loud: water-shallow +6, leaves +7, gravel and metal grates +8, bone litter +9, scattered glass +14. varianceDb is the step-to-step spread: smooth surfaces barely vary, loose ones (gravel, leaves, bone, glass) up to 3. Hollow boards creak: 10% of steps add 12 dB (the bead's creaky board; the seeded roll belongs to the footstep noise rule, mw-e09.5). Wet and frozen modifiers are the controller profile's stealth.surfaces. A material's own footstepLoudness still sets the ground collider's offset; this table is what a scene's tagged surface regions read.
